title: 观猎
author: 王维
intro: Bowstrings sing in a hard wind as a general rides out hunting. Wang Wei, best known for quiet landscapes, here writes something fast, loud and full of energy — and ends on a wide, calm sky.
analysis: 这首诗写一位将军在渭城郊外打猎。一开头先写声音：风很猛，角弓的弦声嗡嗡作响，然后才说出“将军猎渭城”，先声夺人。第二联是名句：秋冬草枯了，老鹰的眼睛看猎物更快更准；雪化了，马跑起来蹄子格外轻快。“疾”和“轻”两个字写出了打猎的速度和兴奋。第三联写将军满载而归，一下子经过新丰，又回到细柳营——“细柳营”是汉代名将周亚夫的军营，暗中称赞这位将军治军严整。最后回头看刚才射雕的地方，只见千里暮云平平地铺在天边。从热闹紧张到开阔平静，节奏一张一弛，很有画面感。“射雕”也暗用了北齐名将“射雕手”的典故，夸将军箭术高超。
analysisEn: A general goes hunting outside Weicheng, near Chang’an. The poem opens with sound before sight: the wind is fierce and the horn-tipped bows twang — only then are we told who it is: “the general hunts at Weicheng.” The second couplet is the most admired: the grass has withered, so the hawk’s eye is quick to spot its prey; the snow has gone, so the horses’ hooves run light. Two single words, 疾 (swift) and 轻 (light), carry all the speed and excitement of the chase. In the third couplet the hunt is over in a flash: they sweep past Xinfeng and are back at Xiliu Camp. Xiliu (“Slender Willow”) was the camp of the Han general Zhou Yafu, famous for strict discipline, so the name quietly praises this general too. Finally he looks back at the place where he shot the eagles, and sees only evening clouds lying flat across a thousand li of sky. After all the noise and speed, the poem ends in wide, still space — tension and release, like a camera pulling back. “Shooting eagles” also recalls a famous Northern Qi general nicknamed the “eagle-shooter”, a compliment to the general’s archery.
background: This is generally thought to be an early work by Wang Wei (701–761), written in his youth or early career; the general is not named. It shows a bold, energetic side of a poet better known for calm landscapes.
pronunciation: 风劲 jìng（不读 jìn）。将军 jiāng。还归 huán。雕 diāo（大型猛禽）。
version: 采用通行版本，与《全唐诗》文本一致；《唐诗三百首》等收录。

lines.lit: The wind is strong; the horn bows twang;
lines.en: In a hard wind the horn bows sing —
the general is hunting outside Weicheng.

lines.lit: The grass is withered; the hawks’ eyes are swift;
lines.en: The grass is dry, and the hawk’s eye is quick;

lines.lit: the snow is gone; the horses’ hooves are light.
lines.en: the snow has melted, and the hooves fly light.
In a flash they are past the market at Xinfeng,
and back again at Slender Willow Camp.

lines.lit: Looking back at the place where eagles were shot,
lines.en: He turns to look where the eagles fell:

lines.lit: for a thousand li the evening clouds lie flat.
lines.en: evening clouds lie level for a thousand miles.

words.note: 现代汉语“强劲”“劲敌”读 jìng；“使劲”读 jìn。
古代用兽角装饰、加固的弓。

words.en: to make a sound (here, the bowstring twanging)

words.note: 古义；今天“疾病”的“疾”意思不同，“疾驰”还保留“快”的意思。
汉代名将周亚夫的军营，以纪律严明著称。
比喻箭术高超；“射雕英雄”今天还常说。

imagery.name: 风
imagery.zh: 强劲的寒风和弓弦声一起，营造出打猎时紧张激烈的气氛。
imagery.en: The hard wind and twanging bows create the tense, exciting atmosphere of the hunt.

imagery.name: 草
imagery.zh: 草枯了，猎物无处藏身，鹰眼显得格外敏锐。
imagery.en: With the grass withered, prey has nowhere to hide, and the hawk’s eye looks sharper than ever.

imagery.name: 雪
imagery.zh: 积雪化尽，马跑得轻快，写出马蹄的速度。
imagery.en: With the snow gone, the horses run light and fast.

imagery.name: 马
imagery.zh: 轻快的马蹄是将军英姿和打猎速度的象征。
imagery.en: The light, flying hooves capture the general’s dash and the speed of the hunt.

imagery.name: 云
imagery.zh: 千里暮云平铺天边，热闹之后归于开阔宁静。
imagery.en: Evening clouds stretched flat for a thousand miles — wide calm after the excitement.
